name: CARROT Weather
tagline: A weather app that reads you the forecast while insulting you, wrapped in very polished native apps, widgets and watch complications.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. CARROT sells tiered subscriptions plus a paid app purchase depending on platform.

verdictSummary: The weather data is not the moat: Open-Meteo hands you hourly, daily and alert data for free with no API key, and an LLM will happily generate sarcastic commentary about 4mm of rain all day long. A one-shot web app gets you the actual loop, current conditions plus a snide remark, in an afternoon. What does not survive is everything CARROT actually charges for: iOS and watchOS widgets, lock screen complications, notification personalities, precipitation alerts that fire before you leave the house, and years of hand written joke variants that do not read like an LLM trying to be funny. If you want a browser tab, build it. If you want a glanceable widget on your wrist, you are signing up for native app work, not a one-shot.
coreLoopDIY: Pulls a forecast for your location from a free weather API and renders it alongside LLM-generated snark tuned to how bad the weather is.
requirements: Open-Meteo (free, no key) for forecast and severe weather alerts
An LLM API key for the commentary, or a hand written joke table if you want it offline and free
Browser geolocation or manually entered coordinates
Optional: RainViewer tiles if you want a radar layer
whatYouLose: Home screen and lock screen widgets, Apple Watch complications, CarPlay, all the glanceable surfaces that are the real product
Push notifications for rain starting in 20 minutes, which needs a server, a scheduler and push credentials you do not have
Hand written comedy with actual voice and range, instead of an LLM producing the same three jokes about drizzle
Radar animation, hourly precipitation graphs, and the pile of secondary data screens that make it feel complete
The silly stuff people stay for: achievements, secret locations, unlockable personalities, the whole game layer
moatNotes: The forecast is a commodity API call. The moat is the writing plus the native surface area on four Apple platforms, which is a lot of grind and not much cleverness.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a weather app is something you look at for four seconds, twelve times a day, and that only works if it lives on your home screen, your lock screen and your watch face. A self-hosted web page fails that test no matter how good the jokes are. People also pay for the writing: a well timed insult about a 5am rain start is a craft product, and an LLM prompted to be sarcastic converges on the same tired register within a week of use.
notes: The forecast is free; the personality and the four native platforms are not.
prompt:
Build a local, single-user snarky weather web app. No accounts, no analytics, no backend database.

Stack, non negotiable: Vite + React + TypeScript, Tailwind for styling, a tiny Node/Express server only as a proxy for the LLM call so the key stays server side. pnpm. Everything runs with one `pnpm dev`.

Data source: Open-Meteo. No API key. Use the forecast endpoint for current conditions, hourly for the next 24 hours, daily for the next 7, plus the geocoding endpoint for location search. Map WMO weather codes to human labels and emoji yourself in a single lookup table.

Core screen, mobile width first:
- Big current temperature, feels-like, condition label, high/low.
- One line of snark under it, generated fresh on each load.
- Horizontal scroll of the next 24 hours: hour, icon, temp, precipitation probability.
- Seven day rows: day, icon, high/low, a thin temperature range bar.
- Location switcher: search box using Open-Meteo geocoding, saved locations in localStorage, plus a "use my location" button via browser geolocation.

Snark engine:
- Server route POST /api/snark takes a compact weather summary (temp, condition, precip chance, wind, whether it is worse or better than yesterday) and returns one sentence.
- Use the Anthropic API, key from .env as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. Include a .env.example.
- System prompt: dry, mean, never cheerful, one sentence, no emoji, no exclamation marks. Vary the angle: the weather itself, the user's plans, the user's life choices.
- Cache the result in localStorage keyed by location plus rounded hour so reloads do not burn tokens.
- If the key is missing, fall back to a hard coded table of at least 30 lines bucketed by condition. The app must be fully usable with no LLM key.

Explicitly out of scope: push notifications, radar maps, widgets, native apps, service worker background sync, multi-user anything. Add a web app manifest and theme color so it can be added to a home screen as a plain PWA shell, nothing more.

Ship a README with setup, the .env keys, and a short honest note that this has no notifications and no widgets.
